title: Concrete Pump Hydraulic Oil Temperature and Cooling
seoTitle: Concrete Pump Oil Temperature & Cooling | ACPA + Pinjin
description: Pinjin does not publish an oil-temperature cut-off or cooler model. ACPA: if hydraulic oil overheats, stop, check the cooler, water box and valve positions, then slow the pump. Burn hazard around 80 °C. Kawasaki pump names on some rows are not thermostat ratings.

answerBlock.what: Hydraulic oil temperature is a safety and reliability limit. Pinjin catalogue rows list motor/engine, output, pressure and, on some models, a Kawasaki hydraulic-pump name. They do not list a maximum oil temperature, cooler type or oil brand. ACPA’s operator study guide: if oil gets hot, stop pumping, check the cooler, find a valve left in the wrong position, confirm the water box is full, mist the tank if needed, then slow the pump. ACPA mechanics: oil can exceed about 176 °F / 80 °C — burn hazard; never work a pressurised leak from below.
answerBlock.who: Operators who see rising oil temperature on a trailer and buyers who asked a marketplace seller for ‘water cooling vs air cooling’ as if it were a Pinjin checkbox.
factors: No Pinjin published oil-temp cut-off — do not invent one
ACPA stop-and-check sequence when oil is hot
Kawasaki 112 / 140 names are pump IDs, not cooler ratings
Persistent overheating may be a developing pump or mix/pipeline problem — not a promised on-site m³/h

faqs.question: What oil temperature is allowed on a Pinjin trailer pump?
faqs.answer: Not published. Catalogue cells are power, output, pressure, hopper, distance, size. ACPA mechanics text warns that oil can get hotter than about 80 °C in a day’s work. Use the ACPA hot-oil sequence; do not treat 80 °C as a Pinjin thermostat setting.

faqs.question: Does the catalogue say water-cooled or air-cooled hydraulics?
faqs.answer: No. Some marketplace listings advertise water-cooling or air-cooling. Pinjin pages that name a hydraulic pump say Kawasaki 112, Kawasaki 140, Kawasaki double pump 100/112/140 — not a cooler type. Ask the factory if you need the cooler arrangement for a listed model; unpublished arrangements are not promised here.

faqs.question: What should the operator do when hydraulic oil is hot?
faqs.answer: ACPA study guide: 1) stop pumping; 2) check the oil cooler (some pumps have a fan override); 3) find the heat source, such as a valve in the wrong position; 4) make certain the water box is full; 5) spray a mist of cool water over the hydraulic system and tank; 6) slow the pumping speed. Repeated overheating can mean a developing machine problem.

image.caption: Diesel 50 — Kawasaki 140 is the printed hydraulic-pump name, not an oil-temperature rating
